symbols.name: A
symbols.role: action set, with \(0\) the reference action

symbols.name: q
symbols.role: maximum outcome lag of an action

symbols.name: Rnodes
symbols.def: \(\mathcal R_0=\{(0,t):t\in[T]\}\) and \(\mathcal R_b=\{(s,\ell,h,a):s\in[T],\;\ell\in\{0,1\},\;s+\ell\le T,\;h\in A^{s-1},\;a\in A\setminus\{0\}\}\), restricted to nodes reached by \(\Pi\).
symbols.role: baseline and history-indexed one-lag blip nodes

symbols.name: d
symbols.def: \(d\) is the number of distinct primitive source occurrences in \(\mathcal R\).
symbols.role: dimension of a unit innovation block

symbols.name: G
symbols.def: The maps \(t:\mathcal R\to[T]\) and \(s:\mathcal R\to[d]\) give the observed outcome time and primitive source label. Edges encode later components subtracted in backward order, and \(c:E\to\mathbb R\), \((r,u)\mapsto c_{ru}\), is known and donor invariant.

symbols.name: I
symbols.def: \(\mathcal I_{r,N}\) contains units whose realized pre-action history and action match the source cell attached to \(r\) in \(\mathcal G\).

symbols.name: gamma
symbols.sig: \(\gamma_{s\ell}(h,a)\in\mathbb R^k\) for admissible \(s\), \(\ell\in\{0,1\}\), \(h\in A^{s-1}\), and \(a\in A\)
symbols.role: history-, action-, time-, and lag-indexed causal blip coefficients

symbols.name: m
symbols.role: causal mean outcome under a treatment history

symbols.name: eta
symbols.def: \(\eta_r\) is the total coefficient of the LTV potential-outcome mean in the donor history cell and outcome time \(t(r)\).

symbols.name: mu
symbols.role: causal baseline or counterfactual blip component at graph node \(r\)

symbols.name: X
symbols.role: noisy factor proxies used by PCR

symbols.name: w
symbols.def: \(w_{ir}\) is the minimum-norm solution of \(\sum_{j\in\mathcal I_{r,N}}w_jv_j=v_i\).

symbols.name: a
symbols.def: \(a_{\pi r}\) is the known incidence with which the baseline or blip node \(r\) contributes to \(\sum_{t=1}^T m_{i0,t}(\pi_{1:t})\).

symbols.name: H
symbols.role: oracle source coefficients from exact donor-invariant backward propagation

symbols.name: Sigma
symbols.role: full donor-reuse covariance and its limit

symbols.name: delta0
symbols.role: class-wide positive lower bound \(\delta_0\) for the proxy-growth exponent

symbols.name: Cclass
symbols.type: fixed finite vector of positive constants
symbols.role: moment, dependence, overlap, loading, coefficient, spectral, effective-rank, and covariance constants shared by every triangular array in the uniform class

symbols.name: rN
symbols.role: common nuisance-error envelope in the proxy-rich sufficient regime

symbols.name: Pclass
symbols.role: common-constant strong-factor one-lag LTV Synthetic-Blips class

symbols.name: A0
symbols.role: shared source in the two-period witness

symbols.name: B0
symbols.role: second source in the two-period witness

symbols.name: C0
symbols.role: third source in the two-period witness

symbols.name: Wit
symbols.def: A legal two-period rank-one one-lag LTV graph with donor-invariant edge coefficients, independent \(A_0,B_0,C_0\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\), and path errors \((A_0,A_0+B_0-C_0)\).

assumptions.condition: \(T\), \(A\), \(k\), \(q=1\), \(d\), \(\mathcal G\), and \(|\Pi|\) do not vary with \(N\).
Inference is conditional on \(D\), \(v\), \(R\), \(\mathcal G\), and the induced donor cells \(I\).
For every feasible \(\bar a_t\), \(m_{it}(\bar a_t)=v_i^{\top}\lambda_t+\sum_{s=\max\{1,t-1\}}^t v_i^{\top}\gamma_{s,t-s}(\bar a_{s-1},a_s)\).

standard.name: one-lag linear time-varying potential-outcome blip model

assumptions.condition: The blocks \(\{\varepsilon_i:i\in[N]\}\) are mutually independent conditional on \(D,v,R,G,I\).
\(c_I N\le|\mathcal I_{r,N}|\le C_I N\) for every \(r\in\mathcal R\).
\(\lambda_{\min}(|\mathcal I_{r,N}|^{-1}\sum_{j\in\mathcal I_{r,N}}v_jv_j^{\top})\ge c_v\) for every \(r\in\mathcal R\).
The conditional proxy-row process \(\{U_{h\cdot}:h\ge1\}\) is absolutely regular with \(\beta_U(m)\le C_\beta\rho^m\), where \(0<\rho<1\).
\(\operatorname{tr}(\mathbb E[U_{h\cdot}^{\top}U_{h\cdot}\mid D,v,R,G,I])\ge c_U N\) for every \(h\in[p]\).

novel.justification: The condition permits correlated measurements across firms while excluding a proxy row driven by only finitely many common noise directions; transaction-category and product-level aggregates with broad firm coverage satisfy this effective-rank geometry.

assumptions.condition: \(p_N\ge\ell_N N^{2+\delta_0}\), where the same \(\delta_0>0\) and \(\ell_N\to\infty\) apply to every array in the class.

novel.justification: This is a deliberately narrow sufficient regime for panels linked to genuinely high-frequency or high-dimensional auxiliary measurements; it is not imposed on applications that contain only the published outcome panel.

standard.name: triangular-array covariance convergence with a common modulus

definitions.name: Uniform one-lag LTV Synthetic-Blips class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P(\mathfrak C,\delta_0,\ell,b_\Sigma)=\{\{P_N,D_N,v_N,R_N,G,I_N\}_{N\ge1}:\text{for every }N,\text{ all listed member properties hold with the same }\mathfrak C,\;\delta_0>0,\;\ell_N\to\infty,\;b_{\Sigma,N}\to0\}\).

definitions.name: Feasible-path causal node map
definitions.construction: For each \(\pi\in\Pi\) and \(t\in[T]\), map the baseline contribution \(v_{i0}^{\top}\lambda_t\) to \((0,t)\), and map each nonzero contribution \(v_{i0}^{\top}\gamma_{s,t-s}(\pi_{1:s-1},\pi_s)\), \(s\in\{t-1,t\}\), to \((s,t-s,\pi_{1:s-1},\pi_s)\). The graph source coefficient \(\eta_r\) is the total LTV coefficient in the matching realized donor cell; reverse subtraction with the donor-invariant \(c_{ru}\) isolates the mapped component \(\beta_r\).

definitions.name: Oracle causal-node recursion
definitions.construction: Traverse \(\mathcal G\) in reverse topological order, use the closed coefficient recursion \(\beta_r=\eta_r-\sum_{u:(r,u)\in E}c_{ru}\beta_u\), and set \(Z_{jr}^{\circ}=Y_{j,t(r)}-\sum_{u:(r,u)\in E}c_{ru}\mu_{ju}\) and \(\widetilde\mu_{ir}=w_{ir}^{\top}Z_{\mathcal I_{r,N},r}^{\circ}+\xi_r^{\top}(X_i-X_{\mathcal I_{r,N}}w_{ir})\).

definitions.name: Row-cross-fitted orthogonal recursive SBE-PCR estimator
definitions.construction: Split the \(p_N\) proxy rows into a fixed number of interlaced blocks separated by mixing gaps. On complementary blocks compute rank-\(k\) leave-one-unit-out PCR weights \(\widehat w_{ir}^{(-f,-i)}\); on an opposite block fit \(\widehat\xi_r^{(f,-i)}\). Traverse \(\mathcal G\) backward using only donor-invariant \(c_{ru}\): \(\widehat Z_{jr}=Y_{j,t(r)}-\sum_{u:(r,u)\in E}c_{ru}\widehat\mu_{ju}\) and \(\widehat\mu_{ir}^{(f)}=(\widehat w_{ir}^{(-f,-i)})^{\top}\widehat Z_{\mathcal I_{r,N},r}+(\widehat\xi_r^{(f,-i)})^{\top}(X_i-X_{\mathcal I_{r,N}}\widehat w_{ir}^{(-f,-i)})\). Average blocks and set \(\widehat V^\pi=\sum_r a_{\pi r}\widehat\mu_{i0,r}\).

definitions.name: Exact donor-invariant backward influence propagation
definitions.construction: Differentiate the finite oracle recursion with coefficient \(c_{ru}\) with respect to every primitive source \(\varepsilon_{i,s(r)}\), retaining each repeated appearance of unit \(i\) at every ancestor node. Aggregate with \(a\) to obtain \(H_{i,N}\) and set \(\Phi_{i,N}=NH_{i,N}\varepsilon_i\).

definitions.name: Orthogonal full-graph remainder handle
definitions.construction: Condition block by block, apply a separated-projector resolvent expansion at each PCR node, use \(R^{\top}\xi_r=\beta_r\) to cancel the donor-weight derivative, control geometrically mixing proxy blocks by coupling, and close the finite backward induction with products of weight, augmentation, projector, and leave-one-unit-out errors.

definitions.name: Weak-proxy frontier handle
definitions.construction: Start from the rank-one equal-loading node and combine a leave-one-row-out spectral resolvent with Berbee blocking for \(\beta\)-mixing proxy rows; compare the resulting remainder envelope with a local loading perturbation whose product distribution has bounded pairwise divergence, then propagate that envelope through the fixed donor-invariant graph.

definitions.name: Leave-one-unit-out full-recursion replay covariance
definitions.construction: For each \(i\), refit every nuisance without unit \(i\), insert its fitted residual block at each source label \(s(r)\) where it appears, replay the entire fitted graph with the same \(c_{ru}\), obtain \(\widehat\Phi_{i,N}\), and set \(\widehat\Sigma_N=N^{-1}\sum_i\widehat\Phi_{i,N}\widehat\Phi_{i,N}^{\top}\).

definitions.name: Gaussian-max bands and maximizing-path set
definitions.construction: Let \(c_{1-\alpha}(\widehat\Sigma_N)\) be the conditional \(1-\alpha\) quantile of \(\max_{\pi\in\Pi}|G^\star_\pi|/\widehat\Sigma_{N,\pi\pi}^{1/2}\). Set \(B_{\pi,N}=[\widehat V^\pi-r_{\pi,N},\widehat V^\pi+r_{\pi,N}]\) and \(\widehat{\mathcal M}_N=\{\pi:\widehat V^\pi+r_{\pi,N}\ge\max_{\rho\in\Pi}(\widehat V^\rho-r_{\rho,N})\}\).

definitions.name: Finite-Gaussian local-gap regret functional
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak R(\Delta,Z)=\Delta_{\operatorname*{argmax}_{\pi\in\Pi}(Z_\pi-\Delta_\pi)}\), with the deterministic tie-breaking rule used by \(\widehat\pi_N\).

definitions.name: Two-period donor-reuse witness
definitions.construction: Use the legal \(T=2\), \(q=1\), rank-one LTV graph \(Wit\), with control and active-action donor histories, donor-invariant edge coefficients, and two path errors \((A_0,A_0+B_0-C_0)\).

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal P(\mathfrak C,\delta_0,\ell,b_\Sigma)\), reverse recursion identifies \(\beta_{(0,t)}=\lambda_t\) and \(\beta_{(s,\ell,h,a)}=\gamma_{s\ell}(h,a)\) at every node reached by \(\Pi\). Consequently \(\mu_{i0,r}\) is the corresponding target-unit counterfactual baseline or blip component and \(V^\pi=\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbb E[Y_{i0,t}(\pi_{1:t})\mid v,D]\).
statements.justification: This result makes the graph value a causal dynamic-path estimand rather than an observed-coordinate prediction.
statements.gap: Agarwal, Han, Saha, Syrgkanis, and Yoon identify path means through LTV blips; this lemma specializes their causal mapping to the fixed finite graph whose full influence law is studied here.
statements.consumer: It validates the welfare interpretation of every coordinate entering schedule comparison.

statements.statement: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P(\mathfrak C,\delta_0,\ell,b_\Sigma)\), \(i\in[N]\), and \(r\in\mathcal R\), \(\|w_{ir}\|_2\le C N^{-1/2}\) and \(\|w_{ir}\|_\infty\le C N^{-1}\). Moreover \(\lambda_{\max}(|\mathcal I_{r,N}|^{-1}\sum_{j\in\mathcal I_{r,N}}v_jv_j^{\top})\le C_v^2\), so no separate upper donor-Gram condition is required.
statements.justification: Class-uniform diffuseness gives a negligible maximum unit influence and derives the redundant Gram upper bound.
statements.gap: Synthetic-Blips PCR consistency does not isolate the uniform source-influence rates required for a joint triangular-array limit.
statements.consumer: The bounds provide Lindeberg and leave-one-unit-out stability inputs for the recursive expansion.

statements.statement: Uniformly over the rank-one equal-loading submodel of \(\mathcal P(\mathfrak C,\delta_0,\ell,b_\Sigma)\), the blocked row-cross-fitted augmented PCR node satisfies \(\widehat\mu_{i0,r}-\mu_{i0,r}=w_{i0,r}^{\top}\varepsilon_{\mathcal I_{r,N}}+o_{\mathbb P}(N^{-1/2})\). The projector error, the donor-weight error after multiplication by \(\sqrt N\), and the augmentation prediction error are each \(O_{\mathbb P}(r_N)\) uniformly, and every cross-fitted nuisance product is \(O_{\mathbb P}(r_N^2)=o_{\mathbb P}(N^{-1/2})\).
statements.justification: This is the early kill test for root-(N) orthogonalization under credible weak proxy-row dependence.
statements.gap: The published SBE proof controls PCR at consistency scale, while generic orthogonal-score theory does not derive the spectral and blocked-row nuisance-product rates.
statements.consumer: Passing the lemma licenses the full finite-graph induction; failure makes the proposed sufficient regime untenable.

statements.statement: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P(\mathfrak C,\delta_0,\ell,b_\Sigma)\), \(\max_{\pi\in\Pi}|\sqrt N(\widehat V^\pi-V^\pi)-N^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^N\Phi_{i,N}^\pi|=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\). The coefficients \(H_{i,N}\) are the exact donor-invariant derivatives of the full causal backward graph and are consistently estimable. This strictly strengthens the pointwise SBE-PCR consistency result of Agarwal, Han, Saha, Syrgkanis, and Yoon by delivering a uniform joint root-\(N\) causal path-vector expansion with recursively reused donors.
statements.justification: The full-graph influence recursion is the load-bearing result that turns identified synthetic-blip paths into jointly regular estimands.
statements.gap: Agarwal, Han, Saha, Syrgkanis, and Yoon prove pointwise consistency, and Synthetic Interventions supplies neither this finite backward recursion nor its shared-donor joint influence coefficients.
statements.consumer: A panel enriched with suitable repeated proxies can compare every prespecified budget-feasible insurance and loan schedule using one coherent uncertainty law.

statements.statement: Determine whether the expansion in \(\mathrm{thm:joint\mbox{-}expansion}\) remains uniform when \(p_N\) grows at or below order \(N^2\) and when proxy rows have slower mixing or low effective rank; characterize the weakest joint frontier in proxy information, spectral separation, and donor diffuseness, and establish failure beyond it by an explicit contiguous rank-one sequence.
statements.justification: The fast-growth regime is only a narrow sufficient envelope, and the practically relevant information boundary remains open.
statements.gap: Robust PCR and low-rank inference do not give a necessity frontier for a target-unit recursive path functional under dependent proxy rows.
statements.consumer: The frontier would determine whether ordinary administrative panels, without massive auxiliary measurements, can support the joint procedure.

statements.statement: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P(\mathfrak C,\delta_0,\ell,b_\Sigma)\), the rectangle distance between the law of \(\sqrt N(\widehat V-V)\) and \(\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_N)\) converges to zero, and \(\Sigma^{-1/2}\sqrt N(\widehat V-V)\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,I_{|\Pi|})\).
statements.justification: The multivariate approximation transfers the recursive influence result to simultaneous comparisons.
statements.gap: Generic Gaussian approximation applies only after the SBE-specific unit influence array and its donor-reuse covariance have been derived.
statements.consumer: It supplies joint critical values for any finite, prespecified schedule menu.

statements.statement: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P(\mathfrak C,\delta_0,\ell,b_\Sigma)\), \(\|\widehat\Sigma_N-\Sigma_N\|_{\mathrm{op}}=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\). Every off-diagonal entry includes all repeated uses of a primitive unit innovation across causal nodes and paths.
statements.justification: Full recursive replay, rather than nodewise residual variance, estimates the covariance actually generated by donor reuse.
statements.gap: Static synthetic-control prediction intervals do not replay a fitted causal backward recursion or recover its cross-path donor-reuse terms.
statements.consumer: The estimator makes the joint influence theorem operational for schedule ranking and simultaneous bands.

statements.statement: For \(Wit\), \(\sqrt N(\widehat V-V)\Rightarrow(A_0,A_0+B_0-C_0)\) and \(\Sigma=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&3\end{pmatrix}\). A diagonal nodewise covariance estimator is therefore inconsistent on a nondegenerate legal one-lag LTV graph.
statements.justification: The witness shows that off-diagonal donor reuse is first order rather than a bookkeeping refinement.
statements.gap: No published Synthetic-Blips result gives a legal recursive covariance calculation even for two periods.
statements.consumer: The construction is a transparent specification check for implementations of recursive replay.

statements.statement: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P(\mathfrak C,\delta_0,\ell,b_\Sigma)\), \(\liminf_N\Pr(V^\pi\in B_{\pi,N}\text{ for all }\pi\in\Pi)\ge1-\alpha\) and \(\liminf_N\inf_{P\in\mathcal P(\mathfrak C,\delta_0,\ell,b_\Sigma)}\Pr(\mathcal M_N\subseteq\widehat{\mathcal M}_N)\ge1-\alpha\).
statements.justification: Band inversion retains every statistically compatible maximizer under exact or local ties.
statements.gap: Inference on Winners targets the parameter attached to a selected coordinate, not the full population argmax set generated by recursive SBE values.
statements.consumer: An analyst can report all undominated prespecified schedules without asserting a noisy unique winner.

statements.statement: Under \(\mathrm{ass:local\mbox{-}gaps}\) and uniformly over its intersection with \(\mathcal P(\mathfrak C,\delta_0,\ell,b_\Sigma)\), \(\sqrt N\operatorname{Reg}_N\Rightarrow\mathfrak R(\Delta,Z)=\Delta_{\operatorname*{argmax}_{\pi\in\Pi}(Z_\pi-\Delta_\pi)}\).
statements.justification: Local ties make schedule regret economically first order even when each path value is regular.
statements.gap: Hirano and Porter study treatment choice in Gaussian limit experiments but do not derive the correlated law induced by recursive synthetic-blip donor reuse.
statements.consumer: The law quantifies the cost of selecting a wrong schedule when causal welfare gaps are on the estimation-noise scale.

sampling_model.design: Conditional triangular-array analysis with deterministic realized treatment paths, latent loadings, proxy coefficients, donor cells, and one fixed causal backward graph.
sampling_model.units: Observed outcome innovation blocks are independent across units and may be dependent across source labels within a unit.
sampling_model.treatment: Potential outcomes obey a genuine time-, lag-, and action-history-indexed one-lag LTV blip model; every feasible path is mapped explicitly to baseline and blip graph nodes.
sampling_model.overlap: Every required history-action donor cell has size proportional to \(N\), with a common positive lower loading-Gram eigenvalue; the upper Gram bound follows from bounded loadings.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Rank-\(k\) PCR weights and row-space coefficients use separated blocks of geometrically \(\beta\)-mixing proxy rows and leave-one-unit-out refits. The sufficient class requires \(p_N\ge\ell_NN^{2+\delta_0}\) with \(\delta_0\ge\underline\delta>0\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper identifies dynamic path means by backward synthetic blips and proves pointwise SBE-PCR consistency.
The paper gives conditions for scalar asymptotic normality of one synthetic-intervention mean with a growing post-period.
The paper combines Neyman orthogonality and cross-fitting to make first-stage effects second order.
The paper uses sample splitting, eigenspace rotation, and refitting for asymptotically normal low-rank inference.
The paper augments synthetic-control weights with an outcome model to correct imperfect balance.
The paper constructs conditional prediction intervals accounting for static weight and post-treatment uncertainty.
The paper proves Gaussian and bootstrap approximation for sums of independent high-dimensional vectors over hyperrectangles.
The paper develops winner's-curse-corrected inference for the parameter attached to a selected option.
The paper derives asymptotically optimal statistical treatment rules through Gaussian limit experiments.
The paper selects policies on a benefit-risk frontier under an available joint Gaussian approximation.
The paper proves finite-sample robustness bounds for principal-component regression with noisy low-rank covariates.
The paper proves Bernstein-type concentration inequalities for weakly dependent sequences.

tldr: For a fixed target unit and a finite menu of dynamic treatment paths, the causal model is a one-lag LTV potential-outcome system whose blips depend on treatment time, lag, action, and realized history. A donor-invariant backward graph maps every path to its counterfactual baseline and blip components. Over an explicit common-constant triangular-array class with geometrically mixing, high-effective-rank proxy rows and the narrow sufficient regime \(p_N\ge\ell_NN^{2+\delta_0}\), the focal result is a uniform joint root-\(N\) influence expansion for the entire causal path vector. A leave-one-unit-out replay of the full graph consistently estimates all donor-reuse covariance terms. Gaussian bands, maximizing-path sets, and local regret are downstream consequences; the weaker proxy-information frontier remains open.

project_justification.gap: Synthetic Blips identifies history-dependent dynamic path means and proves pointwise SBE-PCR consistency, but it does not derive a joint source recursion, a root-(N) path-vector law, or covariance terms created when the same donor innovation is reused across nodes.
project_justification.niche: The technically credible first regime fixes the horizon, graph, rank, and path menu, uses a common positive spectral separation, and links the panel to many weakly dependent, high-effective-rank proxy rows. It is narrower than the empirical data used in the published Korean illustration.
project_justification.fill: The project maps potential-outcome blips to graph nodes, closes the algebra with donor-invariant propagation coefficients, proves orthogonal nuisance products negligible uniformly over the explicit class, and estimates the resulting full covariance by recursive residual replay.

related_work: Agarwal, Han, Saha, Syrgkanis, and Yoon (2025) provide the causal LTV identification and SBE-PCR consistency anchor; the focal theorem strictly strengthens their pointwise consistency result only in the stated fixed finite, proxy-rich regime by adding a joint recursive influence law. Agarwal, Shah, and Shen (2024) inform the scalar PCR limit step, but their growing-post-period Synthetic-Interventions theorem is not a recursive path-vector comparator. Agarwal, Shah, Shen, and Song (2019) inform robust PCR perturbation bounds. Chernozhukov et al. (2018) and Chernozhukov, Hansen, Liao, and Zhu (2023) inform orthogonal cross-fitting and separated low-rank refitting. Merlevède, Peligrad, and Rio (2011) provide concentration tools for weakly dependent proxy rows. Ben-Michael, Feller, and Rothstein (2021) motivate static outcome-model augmentation. Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021) separate static weight and prediction uncertainty but do not replay a causal graph. Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2017) supply Gaussian approximation after the unit influence array exists. Andrews, Kitagawa, and McCloskey (2024) and Hirano and Porter (2009) inform, respectively, winner inference and local treatment-choice analysis; those selection results are downstream here.
technical_internal_limitation: The proxy-rich condition \(p_N\ge\ell_NN^{2+\delta_0}\) is only a narrow sufficient regime. The published Korean export-insurance and loan application does not itself contain the required massive repeated proxy measurements, so the proposed inference cannot be claimed for that data set without a new administrative, transaction, shipment, remote-sensing, or text linkage. Weak factors, rank uncertainty, a growing horizon, and a growing path menu are excluded.
honest_scope: The causal LTV mapping and donor-invariant oracle source recursion are settled algebraic targets. The load-bearing open proof is uniform root-\(N\) equivalence between feasible blocked row-cross-fitted PCR and that oracle recursion under the explicit common-constant class; replay covariance is the second novel theorem. Simultaneous bands, maximizer-set coverage, and local regret follow only after those two results. The weaker \(p_N\) and dependence frontier is an open-ended question. With \(T=2\) and no donor reuse, the influence map reduces to the scalar Synthetic-Interventions decomposition; the legal shared-source graph instead gives \(\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&3\end{pmatrix}\).

novelty_justification: The closest comparator identifies one-lag LTV Synthetic-Blips path means and proves pointwise SBE-PCR consistency. The focal theorem strictly tightens that result on an explicit fixed finite, proxy-rich subclass by deriving a joint root-\(N\) influence array from the complete donor-invariant causal recursion. The companion replay theorem consistently estimates covariance created by repeated primitive donor innovations, an object absent from scalar Synthetic-Interventions limits and static synthetic-control intervals.

_pre_d0_cursor.topic: Joint influence recursion and selection-valid path inference for LTV Synthetic-Blips panels. Fix one target unit, finite T and action set, q=1, fixed latent rank, and a finite budget-feasible path class. Conditional on deterministic LTV latent factors and assignments, let every required action-time donor cell grow proportionally to N; impose independent cross-unit sub-Gaussian innovations with bounded fourth moments, separated normalized factor/loading Grams, row-space inclusion and donor exogeneity, diffuse minimum-norm donor weights, p_N/N^(2+delta)->infinity noisy factor covariates, and a positive-definite limiting oracle covariance. Construct a covariate-row-cross-fitted orthogonal recursive SBE-PCR estimator with an explicit computable unit influence array and uniform joint root-N expansion for all target path values. Prove a multivariate Gaussian approximation and uniform consistency of covariance obtained by replaying the fitted recursion on leave-one-out residuals, including off-diagonal donor-reuse terms; then derive simultaneous path bands, an honest maximizing-path set, and the finite-Gaussian local-gap regret law. Consumer: Synthetic Blips' Korean export-insurance/loan schedule and targeting analysis. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The oracle source coefficients can be propagated exactly through the finite backward graph: each blip-node coefficient equals its donor-weighted observed-outcome coefficient minus propagated baseline and later-blip coefficients. This gives Phi_{r,N}^pi=N H_r^pi epsilon_r and Sigma_N=N sum_r H_r H_r' Var(epsilon_r). In the legal T=2 LTV witness with control, time-1 action, and time-2 action cells, the two path errors are (A,A+B-C), yielding Sigma=[[1,1],[1,3]] without cancellation. A separated rank-k spectral projector is differentiable. Row-space augmentation w'Z+xi'(X_i-X_S w), with xi estimated on opposite covariate-row folds and unit leave-out, makes the population derivative in w vanish, suggesting only nuisance-product remainders remain when p_N/N^(2+delta)->infinity. Checks found no collision with Synthetic Interventions scalar CLTs or dynamic softmax inference, and fixed spectral margins avoid projector boundary nonregularity. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove uniformly that the orthogonalized finite leave-one-out PCR recursion differs from its oracle version by o_P(N^(-1/2)), controlling spectral derivatives and every cross-fitted augmentation product. EARLY KILL TEST: At one rank-one equal-loading donor node with p_N=N^(2+delta), prove the augmented estimator's oracle expansion and influence-coefficient consistency uniformly; pivot if either root-N remainder fails under the stated gap and diffuseness.

message: Revised and validated the full proposal core, repairing the causal LTV model, donor-invariant recursion, uniform triangular-array class, weakly dependent proxy regime, donor-Gram assumptions, and application scope while preserving the joint influence and replay-covariance kernel.
